microtheory.name: pharmacology
microtheory.definition: Pharmacology — drug action. Pharmacokinetics (what body does to drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion — ADME) + pharmacodynamics (what drug does to body: receptor interaction, dose-response). Drug discovery, classification by mechanism, adverse effects, drug interactions. Substrate analogue: applied biochemistry of intervention in biological-system dynamics.

concepts.name: drug
concepts.definition: Substance modifying biological function. Therapeutic, recreational, performance-enhancing. Distinct from food + poison by intent + dose.

concepts.name: pharmacokinetics
concepts.definition: PK. ADME: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion. What body does to drug. Substrate analogue: substrate's processing of input over time.

concepts.name: pharmacodynamics
concepts.definition: PD. What drug does to body. Receptor binding, dose-response, efficacy. Substrate analogue: substrate's response to drug-input.

concepts.name: absorption_pk
concepts.definition: Drug entering systemic circulation. Oral (first-pass through liver), IV, IM, topical, inhaled. Bioavailability fraction reaching circulation.

concepts.name: distribution_pk
concepts.definition: Drug movement to tissues. Volume of distribution = apparent volume. Protein binding affects free fraction.

concepts.name: metabolism_pk
concepts.definition: Drug breakdown. Phase I (CYP450 oxidation) + Phase II (conjugation). Hepatic primarily.

concepts.name: excretion_pk
concepts.definition: Drug elimination. Renal (urine) + biliary (feces). Half-life from clearance + volume of distribution.

concepts.name: half_life
concepts.definition: t½. Time for plasma concentration to halve. Determines dosing interval. Steady state after ~5 half-lives.

concepts.name: receptor
concepts.definition: Macromolecule binding drug + transducing effect. GPCRs, ion channels, enzymes, nuclear receptors. Substrate analogue: substrate's reception node.

concepts.name: agonist
concepts.definition: Activates receptor. Full agonist (max efficacy), partial (sub-max), inverse (reduces constitutive activity).

concepts.name: antagonist
concepts.definition: Blocks receptor. Competitive (reversible, surmountable) vs non-competitive. β-blockers, antihistamines.

concepts.name: dose_response
concepts.definition: Effect vs dose. Sigmoidal. EC50 + Emax characterise. Therapeutic window = effective + non-toxic range.

concepts.name: potency_efficacy
concepts.definition: Potency = dose for given effect (lower = more potent). Efficacy = maximum effect (higher = more efficacious). Distinct.

b.value: dose for given effect (lower = more potent)

concepts.name: therapeutic_index
concepts.definition: LD50/ED50 (lethal vs effective dose). Wider = safer. Lithium, digoxin narrow → blood-level monitoring.

concepts.name: drug_classes
concepts.definition: By mechanism + indication: antibiotics, antihypertensives, statins, NSAIDs, opioids, antidepressants, antipsychotics, chemotherapeutics.

concepts.name: antibiotic_pharm
concepts.definition: Kills/inhibits bacteria. β-lactams (cell wall), aminoglycosides (ribosome), fluoroquinolones (DNA gyrase). Resistance major problem.

concepts.name: nsaid
concepts.definition: COX inhibitor. Reduces prostaglandins → analgesic + antipyretic + anti-inflammatory. GI + renal + cardiac adverse effects.

concepts.name: opioid
concepts.definition: μ-receptor agonist. Powerful analgesic. Highly addictive (reward + tolerance + withdrawal). Public health crisis.

concepts.name: ssri
concepts.definition: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. First-line antidepressant. Increases synaptic serotonin. Fluoxetine, sertraline, escitalopram.

concepts.name: statin
concepts.definition: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. Lowers LDL cholesterol. Reduces cardiovascular events.

concepts.name: drug_discovery
concepts.definition: Target identification → hit-to-lead → optimisation → preclinical → clinical (phases I-IV). 10-15 years, $1B+, ~10% success.

concepts.name: clinical_trial_phases
concepts.definition: Phase I (safety, healthy volunteers); II (efficacy + dose-finding); III (RCT vs standard); IV (post-marketing surveillance).

concepts.name: structure_activity_relationship
concepts.definition: SAR. How structural changes affect activity. Foundation of medicinal chemistry.

concepts.name: adverse_drug_reaction
concepts.definition: ADR. Unwanted drug effect. Type A (predictable from pharmacology) vs Type B (idiosyncratic). Pharmacovigilance.

concepts.name: drug_interaction
concepts.definition: One drug affects another. PK (e.g., CYP inhibition/induction) or PD (additive/antagonistic). Polypharmacy increases risk combinatorially.

concepts.name: drug_resistance
concepts.definition: Reduced effect over time/exposure. Antibiotic resistance via selection; cancer chemotherapy via mutation; tolerance via receptor downregulation.

concepts.name: addiction
concepts.definition: Compulsive drug-seeking despite harm. Substrate of reward pathways (mesolimbic dopamine). Distinct from physical dependence.

concepts.name: pharmacogenomics
concepts.definition: Genetic variation affecting drug response. CYP2D6 + 2C19 + TPMT. Precision medicine via dosing.

concepts.name: biologics
concepts.definition: Protein-based drugs. Monoclonal antibodies, recombinant proteins. Trastuzumab, rituximab, adalimumab. Distinct from small molecules.

concepts.name: small_molecule_drug
concepts.definition: Synthetic chemicals <900 Da. Oral typically. Cross membranes, may cross blood-brain barrier.

concepts.name: antibody_drug_conjugate
concepts.definition: ADC. Antibody targeting + cytotoxic payload. Trastuzumab emtansine. Combines specificity + potency.

rules.name: adme_governs_pharmacokinetics
rules.head: Jabberwock predicts drug concentration over time
rules.body: absorption + distribution + metabolism + excretion together determine plasma profile. Half-life sets dosing interval. Volume of distribution sets loading dose.

rules.name: receptor_binding_drives_pharmacodynamics
rules.head: Jabberwock models drug effect
rules.body: drug binds receptor → transduction → biological response. Dose-response sigmoidal with EC50 + Emax. Selectivity vs off-target effects.

rules.name: therapeutic_window_constrains_dosing
rules.head: Jabberwock prescribes a drug
rules.body: must achieve effective without reaching toxic concentration. Narrow therapeutic index drugs require monitoring.

rules.name: pharmacogenomics_personalises_dosing
rules.head: Jabberwock predicts patient drug response
rules.body: genetic variation in metabolising enzymes (CYP2D6, CYP2C19) explains differential response. Dose adjustment per genotype.

rules.name: drug_interaction_combinatorial_risk
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates polypharmacy
rules.body: interaction risk grows combinatorially with drug count. Common via CYP inhibition/induction. Elderly especially vulnerable.
